---
title: "Blood–Brain Barrier Gene Conservation Across Human, Mouse, and Macaque"
subtitle: "A quantitative analysis of coding-sequence conservation and selection pressure in BBB genes vs. liver controls."
toc: false
page-layout: article
---

::: {.hub-summary}

Drugs for the brain are tested in mice, then macaques, then people — and every arrow in
that chain is a translational leap. This project asks how well that chain holds at the DNA
level: **how conserved are blood–brain barrier genes across the three species?** Each gene
is measured two ways — **% nucleotide identity**, how many DNA letters match, and
**dN/dS**, whether evolution is actively removing protein-changing mutations — against a
control set of genes from a tissue that is not the brain.

The headline is a method result rather than a biological one. **Macaque coding sequence is
far closer to human than mouse is, and gene duplication is what drives real divergence**:
where mouse has two copies of a gene humans have once (*Abcb1a* and *Abcb1b* for human
*ABCB1*), identity collapses to ~47% against ~85% for clean one-to-one pairs — a large,
robust effect. The tissue-level claim that would have been the headline — that BBB genes
are under stronger purifying selection than liver genes — **does not currently stand**, and
[the audit](audit.qmd) explains exactly why: the liver control was never filtered, so 86.6%
of it is brain-expressed too.

:::

## Key results

::: {.hub-figs}

![**Macaque sits closer to human than mouse, gene for gene.** Each point is one BBB gene, plotted by its human–mouse identity against its human–macaque identity. Note the 224 one-to-one macaque pairs falling below 85% — those are an artefact of the longest-transcript heuristic, not biology.](images/translational-ladder.png){group="key"}

![**Distribution of % nucleotide identity, BBB genes against the liver control.** The two distributions sit almost on top of one another. Under the orthologue rule actually used, BBB scored *below* the control (84.12 vs 84.32); applying one rule to both sides reverses it (85.04 vs 84.47). The comparison is not currently trustworthy in either direction.](images/pid-density.png){group="key"}

:::

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## These figures are provisional

Three upstream steps — `step1` (wrong source tables), `step4c` (the liver filter never ran)
and `step5d` (different orthologue rules on the two sides) — feed everything shown here. No
figure on this site should be cited until they are fixed and steps 5c–5h re-run.
[What's wrong, in full →](audit.qmd)
:::

## About this project

Undergraduate research project by **Yara Ismail**, under the supervision of
**Dr. Claire Clelland**. The pipeline is written in R against Ensembl release 113, the Human
Protein Atlas, and five published transcriptomic datasets. Everything — data, scripts, and
this site — is in the
[GitHub repository](https://github.com/Mmynemious/BBB-Gene-Conservation).
